Before applying this update, make sure all previously released errata relevant to your system have been applied.

For details on how to apply this update, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258
portal_description:
The Pacemaker cluster resource manager is a collection of technologies working together to maintain data integrity and application availability in the event of failures.

This update fixes the following bugs:

* Previously, if the cluster connection to the Pacemaker Remote service node was moving from one cluster node to another, and a clone on the Pacemaker Remote node required notifications, the cluster could get stuck in a loop preventing the actions from completing. With this update, the actions proceed normally in this situation and the described problem no longer occurs. (BZ#1646347)

* Previously, a guest node or bundle instance had to be unmanaged before cleaning, otherwise it would get restarted. With this update, the managed instances can be cleaned without problems. (BZ#1646350)

* Previously, clusters that used storage-based death (SBD) for fencing
could not configure guest nodes or bundles. As a consequence, the
guest node or bundle instance would be restarted if any resource running
on it needed to contact the cluster daemons. With this update, clusters with SBD can configure guest nodes and bundles and the described problem no longer occurs. (BZ#1646872)

Users of pacemaker are advised to upgrade to these updated packages, which fix these bugs.
